subject: Proposal: Milestone-driven co-term with escrowed credit bucket

Subject: Proposal: Milestone-driven co-term with escrowed credit bucket

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for a constructive renewal conversation last week. Based on the usage profile you shared and the expansion you described, attached is a draft SOW that moves your renewal to a co-termed, milestone-driven structure that we think will reduce upfront commitment friction while giving BluePeak predictable unit economics as you scale. Key points: 

- Term: 30 months co-term to your FY end (co-term date: 2028-12-31)
- Commit structure: Annual committed token bucket with three trigger milestones tied to actual usage (25%, 60%, 100% of annual commit)
- Escrowed credits: A short-term escrow (20% of year-1 commit) held as credits that are released to your invoice as each milestone is achieved to avoid large immediate overages
- Billing cadence: Quarterly invoices with credits applied as offsets; unused escrow credits roll forward for 12 months
- Ramp assistance: We will provide two free onboarding days and a 30% professional services credit to accelerate model migration

I attached BP_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf and a usage excerpt I pulled for Mar–May 2027. Can you confirm whether BluePeak Procurement is comfortable with credits held in escrow and released on milestones, or would they prefer an invoice-credit model instead? Also confirm the co-term date (we proposed 2028-12-31 to align with your FY).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Sophie: confirm procurement preference and co-term date
2) Marissa: we'll circulate a redline-ready contract and a DocuSign link once procurement confirms
3) Karthik: if procurement wants invoice-credit accounting rather than escrow, can you confirm how we'd amortize credits on our side?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

Hi Sophie / Procurement team — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and proposed mechanics below (Karthik is copied for pricing/accounting confirmation):

1) Escrow mechanics: Redwood would hold the escrow as a contractual credit balance on our platform tied to the account (not with a third party). That balance is 100% earmarked to BluePeak and appears on invoices as a separate line item "Escrow credit applied." The credits are applied automatically when the usage milestone clears.

2) Invoice appearance / P&L: Credits will appear as invoice line-item offsets (not rebates). For your internal finance teams, we can provide a monthly export that shows gross charges and credit offsets to make reconciliation straightforward. 

3) Grace window: We propose a soft-trigger +/- 5% window on milestone thresholds with a 30-day cure period. If you cross below the milestone beyond that window for the year, credits remain but no further escrow releases occur until the next milestone is met.

Milestone schedule (proposed):
- Milestone A: 25% of annual commit — release 40% of escrowed credits 30 days after met
- Milestone B: 60% of annual commit — release 40% of escrowed credits 30 days after met
- Milestone C: 100% of annual commit — remaining 20% released 30 days after met

Pricing summary (high level):
- Base committed rate: $0.0045 / 1K tokens for year 1 (with volume tier to $0.0038 at > 3x baseline usage)
- Escrow amount: 20% of year-1 committed spend (held as credits)

Karthik — can you confirm the accounting flow for Redwood if we apply credits this way and whether we need to build a special invoice code? Also flag any SLA credit language we should attach in the SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment(s): usage_report_Mar-May2027.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing & accounting notes for BluePeak structure

Marissa / Grace — quick internal note so we're aligned before procurement signs: 
- Accounting: We will record the escrowed credits as a deferred liability on Redwood's books until released. When released, credits are applied to the customer's invoice as an offset line (not as a discount). We should create invoice code "ESC-APPL" to make AR reporting and HubSpot reconciliation easier.
- Billing cadence: Quarterly invoices per the SOW; credits applied in the quarter following milestone clearance (30-day lag).
- Credit amount: For the proposed 20% escrow, estimate initial escrow value $120k (based on committed spend in SOW). 
- SLA protections: propose a 10% credit to customer if quarterly p95 latency exceeds 2s for >3 incidents; this credit reduces future escrow releases by the credited amount (to preserve net economics).
- Legal: Grace please add standard clawback language in the SOW for misuse of credits and a 12-month roll-forward cap.

If this looks good I'll finalize the invoice code request with Finance and push the redline SOW to DocuSign after procurement confirms.
- Karthik
